newsitem.title: USA: Dlr surges above 1.80 marks, sets new 71-mo high.
newsitem.headline: Dlr surges above 1.80 marks, sets new 71-mo high.

text.p: The dollar popped briefly above the 1.80 mark threshold for the first time in nearly six years on Tuesday, cheered by persistent mark weakness on the crosses but jittery over prospects for central bank intervention, dealers said.
"I think clearly there was large option interest, barriers, knockouts, the whole nine yards that were so magnetic to that 1.80 level," said Rob Sabia, vice president at ING Barings Capital Markets.
"Everybody has been talking about this for days and days," he added. "It was something that people wanted to see print, they needed to get a print and they printed it."
The dollar rose as high as 1.8004 marks in the U.S. morning, before shrinking back quickly shortly thereafter.
Given lingering talk of central bank intervention, traders said the rate could now be vulnerable to profit-taking.
"If we start to trade back below 1.7940, I think people who have built up long dollar positions will start taking profits," said Sabia. "They will say the target has been achieved."
The dollar shrank to a low of 1.7830 in overseas trade after German finance minister Theo Waigel called recent dollar strength an overreaction.
But it battled back in the U.S. morning, supported by persistent mark weakness against sterling and continental European currencies.
Expectations of a weak euro and persistent sluggishness in the German economy also continued to take their toll on the mark.
